posts.title: Ivermectin–Mebendazole Cancer Paper to Date Finds 37 Distinct Anticancer Mechanisms Across 25 Human Cancer Types

link_metadata.description: Abstract Background. Ivermectin and mebendazole are generic, orally administered anti-infective agents that appear on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines, carry decades of human safety data from hundreds of millions of administrations, and have each accumulated substantial evidence of antineoplastic activity. Existing reviews address monotherapy, emphasize mechanistic preclinical data, and predate a considerable body of clinical data published between 2021 and 2026. We set out to review the mechanistic, laboratory, and clinical data of ivermectin-mebendazole as adjunctive, combination therapy in patients undergoing conventional cancer care. Methods. PubMed, Europe PMC and Google Scholar were searched through October 2026 for peer-reviewed in vitro, in vivo, and human studies of ivermectin and mebendazole in malignant disease, supplemented by oncology meeting abstracts, reference-list screening of prior reviews and ClinicalTrials.gov records.
